title: Past storm speed gave no clear gain in next-day Atlantic wind-change estimates for offshore windows in 2003-2023
abstract: We tested whether past storm speed improves next-day wind-change estimates in selected offshore North Atlantic windows. We used IBTrACS v04r01 and fitted each test season from earlier seasons. The 2003-2023 test has 1,655 windows from 133 storms. Adding prior 12-hour speed and its square to a model with position, season, initial wind and prior wind change increased mean squared error by 0.48%. The conditional 95% interval for error reduction was -1.84% to +0.55%. All planned sample and speed checks had intervals that included zero. The result gives no clear extra prediction value for these speed terms. It does not rule out an ocean-cooling effect. Future eligibility, revised tracks, simple models and 21 test seasons limit use. The package includes a frozen source subset, code, every test estimate, resampling draws, an independent audit and a figure.

display.caption: Adding past speed gave no clear MSE reduction. Bars show conditional 95% limits from three-year block resampling of test-season errors. Positive values mean lower error. The right panel includes prior wind change in each baseline.
